    <title>Axioms for graph clustering quality functions</title>
    <updated>2014-07-22T16:22:29Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.3383v2" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/1308.3383v2" rel="related" type="application/pdf" title="pdf"/>
    <summary>We investigate properties that intuitively ought to be satisfied by graph clustering quality functions, that is, functions that assign a score to a clustering of a graph. Graph clustering, also known as network community detection, is often performed by optimizing such a function. Two axioms tailored for graph clustering quality functions are introduced, and the four axioms introduced in previous work on distance based clustering are reformulated and generalized for the graph setting. We show that modularity, a standard quality function for graph clustering, does not satisfy all of these six properties. This motivates the derivation of a new family of quality functions, adaptive scale modularity, which does satisfy the proposed axioms.
